question.text: If USDINR spot is 83 and 1-year futures is 84.58, using the approximate forward-premium formula, what is the implied interest rate differential between India and USA?

explanation.text: The Logic: The approximate forward-premium formula is (F - S)/S x 100 = (84.58 - 83)/83 x 100 = 1.58/83 x 100 = 1.9036%, or approximately 1.90%. This is the value the stem specifies and the value the workbook uses on pp.62-63 to convert a forward premium to an implied interest-rate differential. The Trap: Option B (1.58%) divides by 100 instead of by the spot rate. Option D (0.83%) is an unrelated distractor. The original ambiguous version had a 2.00% distractor which was also source-supported: the same workbook example derives the 84.5809 futures price from India 7% and USA 5% via exact IRP, giving a 2% rate spread. By specifying the approximate-formula method and replacing the 2.00% distractor, the question is now unambiguous. Note: The original question was ambiguous because (F-S)/S gives 1.90% while the same source example's stated rate spread is 2.00%, both defensible. The stem has been tightened to "using the approximate forward-premium formula" and the 2.00% distractor has been replaced with 2.50% so option A is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series I (Currency Derivatives, Dec 2025), pp.62-63.
